release.name: The Hunt for Stanley 2026 Debut Pack
release.description:
Sale Starts: Tuesday June 2, 2026 at 1pm ET / 10am PT

 

Price: $12 USD

# Packs Available: 1500 packs total. Edition numbers are distributed randomly.

 

Purchase Limit: Ten (10) pack limit per person for the first 6 hours; the limit increases to a fifty (50) pack limit per person afterward. Once the “Buy Now” process has started, users will have 10 minutes to complete checkout before the pack(s) is released for another collector to purchase.

 

Highlights Per Pack: 5

Pack Contents (Highlight Rarity, Edition Size):

  • One (1) highlight from The Hunt for Stanley 2026 (Limited #/500)
  • Two (2) highlights with the following probabilities:
    • 50% Playoff Bound 2026 (Core #/1500)
    • 20% Base 2025-26 (Core #/1500)
    • 20% The Hunt for Stanley 2026 (Limited #/500)
    • 10% Opening Ice 2025-26 (Rare #/250)
  • One (1) highlight with the following probabilities:
    • 75% Base 2025-26 (Core #/1500)
    • 22% Opening Ice 2025-26 (Rare #/250)
    • 3% Making the Mark 2025-26 (Epic #/100)
  • One (1) highlight with the following probabilities:
    • 49% Base 2025-26 (Core #/1500)
    • 20% Filthy Apples (Limited #/500)
    • 20% The Hunt for Stanley 2026 (Limited #/500)
    • 7.93% Seasoned Steel (Rare #/250)
    • 1.5% Making the Mark 2025-26 (Epic #/100)
    • 1.5% Conn Smythe Showcase (Epic #/100)
    • 0.07% The Greatest Achievements (Legendary #/10)

Highlights List

 

Payment Methods Accepted: Most major credit and debit cards. Payments will be processed via Stripe. 

 

Fan Marketplace: Packs and highlights are eligible to be sold to other collectors in the NHL Breakaway fan marketplace. See FAQ.

 

Transferability: Packs and highlights can be exchanged in the Trade Lounge™ with other NHL Breakaway users.

 

Blockchain: Polygon

 

Collection Guarantee: Series 3 highlights will only be distributed during Series 3, which ends prior to the start of the 2026-27 Regular Season. We will not issue more than the edition limit we have set. Any editions not distributed in packs will not be distributed after the series end date (See FAQ for “Uncirculated Editions”)

summary.name: Jacob Fowler
summary.description:
Jacob Fowler, the Canadiens’ third round pick in the 2023 NHL Draft, earned his first career NHL win in style. The Melbourne, Florida native stopped 36 shots in his first NHL start, backstopping the Canadiens to a 4-2 road victory over Pittsburgh.
The rookie goaltender was named First Star of the game after turning aside every key chance in a tightly contested matchup, giving Montreal a big two points on the road.

summary.name: Anton Frondell
summary.description:
Anton Frondell, the 3rd overall pick in the 2025 NHL Draft, made his mark in front of the home crowd at the United Center. On just his second shift of the game, the 18-year-old Swedish center tracked down a loose puck chopped in front and pounced on the rebound, snapping it home in the first period for his first career NHL goal.

summary.name: Porter Martone
summary.description:
Fresh off a faceoff win in the offensive zone in overtime, the Flyers set up on a 5-on-3 power play. Christian Dvorak fed Porter Martone in the high slot, and the 6th overall pick in the 2025 NHL Draft wired a shot that was kicked out before the 19-year-old rookie pounced on the rebound and banged it home at 2:31 for his first career NHL goal.
The Peterborough product’s overtime winner lifted Philadelphia to a huge 2-1 victory during their playoff push.

summary.name: Carter Yakemchuk
summary.description:
Carter Yakemchuk, the 7th overall pick in the 2024 NHL Draft, stepped up from the blue line and delivered in his NHL debut. Fresh off a faceoff win in the offensive zone, the Senators worked the puck back to the point where the 20-year-old Alberta product skated into the right circle and wired a snap shot glove side in the second period for his first career NHL goal.
The big defenseman’s tally helped Ottawa build a lead in their eventual 3-2 victory over Detroit.

summary.name: Noah Östlund
summary.description:
Noah Östlund, the 16th overall pick in the 2022 NHL Draft, finally broke through for his first career NHL goal in his 13th game. The Swedish center worked a smooth give-and-go with Isak Rosen, firing his first attempt just wide. Right after the miss, Rosen fed him again from behind the net, and Östlund roofed it home to tie the game in the third period.

summary.name: Martin Necas
summary.description:
Martin Necas reaches 100 points.  
Late in the third period with the net empty, Necas picked up the puck in his own zone and delivered a clean breakout pass. That assist on the empty-net goal gave him his 100th point of the 2025-26 season — the first time he’s hit the century mark in his NHL career.  
Necas finished the night with the milestone in a 3-1 Avalanche road win, wrapping up a tremendous campaign of 38 goals and 62 assists through 78 games.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Patrick Kane
summary.description:
In a milestone-filled stretch, Patrick Kane scored twice to reach the 500-goal plateau — becoming just the fifth United States-born player to accomplish the feat and the 50th player in NHL history to do so.  
Goal No. 499 came in the final minute of the first period, as Kane cashed in on a 5-on-3 power play for the Red Wings. Then in the third, with the home crowd in Detroit on its feet, he sent an empty-netter into the cage to secure career goal No. 500 and put the game away.  
The milestone tally came just weeks before Kane later surpassed Mike Modano for the most points in NHL history by a U.S.-born player — two landmark moments in a season that further cemented his legacy as one of the greatest American players the game has ever seen.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Nick Suzuki
summary.description:
In the second period against the Islanders, Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki took a feed from close range and snapped home his 29th goal of the season at 15:56, breaking the ice in what turned into a 4-1 Montreal victory. That tally pushed the center to his 100th point of the 2025-26 campaign, the first time he has ever reached the century mark in his NHL career.  
Suzuki added an assist just moments later and closed the season with 29 goals and 72 assists for 101 points in 82 games. The milestone also made him the first Montreal player to hit 100 points since 1986.

summary.name: Conn Smythe Showcase
summary.description: Conn Smythe Showcase stands as a timeless collection of defining highlights from past Conn Smythe Trophy winners. Relive the clutch goals, game-saving stops, and pivotal plays that earned these players playoff MVP honors and cemented their championship legacy.

summary.name: Wayne Gretzky
summary.description:
On December 30, 1981, Wayne Gretzky delivered a performance for the ages, etching his name even deeper into hockey history. Facing the Philadelphia Flyers at Northlands Coliseum, Gretzky erupted for an incredible five-goal night, reaching the unprecedented milestone of 50 goals in just 39 games. Each goal told a story: his first two came in the opening period to set the tone, his third helped Edmonton reclaim a two-goal advantage in the second, his fourth—the game-winning goal—highlighted his clutch play, and his fifth, an empty-netter with seconds remaining, sent the Edmonton Oilers faithful into a frenzy as "The Great One" shattered the NHL’s previous record of 50 goals in 50 games.  
At just 20 years old, Gretzky’s achievement showcased his unparalleled scoring ability, vision, and dominance over the game. That season, he would go on to set a staggering 92-goal record, solidifying his place as one of hockey's most extraordinary talents. Gretzky’s 50-in-39 remains a defining moment in the sport’s history—a feat that redefined the limits of greatness and further established his legacy as a generational icon.
